title: Excavations
whatItIs: Every year people are killed or seriously injured in excavations: by collapsing sides, falling materials, falls into the hole and contact with buried or overhead services.

keyFacts.text: All practicable steps MUST be taken, with supports or battering where needed, so no one is buried or trapped.
A competent person MUST inspect a supported or battered excavation each shift and after any fall or event.
Steps MUST be taken to stop people, work equipment and materials falling into an excavation.

keyFacts: Keep spoil, plant and vehicles back from the edge: the extra load can make the sides collapse.
Access ladders: on a firm level base, secured against slipping, and at least 1 m above the landing.
Don't run petrol or diesel engines in or near an excavation: exhaust fumes can collect in it.

visual.caption: Plan for these before digging starts (HSG150 para 341)

items.title: Collapse of the sides
items.text: Support with trench sheets, boxes or props, or batter the sides back to a safe angle.

items.title: Falls into the excavation
items.text: Guard rails and toe boards, or trench sheets or box sides above ground level.

items.title: Vehicles and materials
items.text: Keep them back from the edge; for tipping, use secured stop blocks a safe distance back.

items.title: Services and water
items.text: Find buried services first; pump water to sumps; keep clear of power lines.

a.label: Inspection (CDM reg 22)
points: Start of every shift, by a competent person
After any event or fall of material

b.label: Report (CDM reg 24)
points: Needed when the inspector isn't satisfied it's safe
Copy within 24 hours; no work until it's fixed

onTheTest.question: When must a supported trench be inspected by a competent person?
options: Only when it is first dug
At the start of every shift and after any event affecting it
onTheTest.why: CDM 2015 reg 22(4): at the start of the shift, after any event likely to affect its strength or stability, and after any material falls or is dislodged.

onTheTest.question: Where should excavated spoil be kept?
options: Right at the edge to save time
Back from the edge, so it can't overload the sides or fall in
In the bottom of the trench
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 350: don't store spoil close to the sides. The extra load can collapse them, and loose material can fall on the people below.

traps: Don't trust the ground: HSE says no ground can be relied on to stand unsupported in all circumstances.
A 'small' fall of soil isn't small: depending on conditions, a cubic metre can weigh over 1.5 tonnes.
Never work ahead of the support or take it out early.
Exposed pipes and cables are not handholds or footholds for climbing out.
